messages:
maya: FYI I kicked off an offline replay set last night to evaluate kernel selection + queue policies against a couple token_budget targets. quick notes below — pasted logs and config.
ashok: awesome — which traces? long-context vs burst small-reqs?
maya: mix of prod traces: 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% mid (64-512), 10% long (512-4096). used same seed as last month for deterministic ordering.
leo: can you paste the replay command and the kernel policy toggles? would like to run a tiny sanity locally.
maya: command:
```
./replay-sim --trace-dir=/traces/2026-02-21 --policy-variants="latency_pref,throughput_mix" --kv-warmup=on --token-budget-targets=8,12,20 --outdir=/tmp/replay-runs/17721
```
maya: highlights:
- latency_pref: lower median but 95p regressed for short requests on GPU A (p95 +120ms)
- throughput_mix: higher batching, better token/sec but p95 worse for mixed workloads
- token_budget 8: lots of micro-batches, higher kernel-switch overhead
- token_budget 12: somewhat sweet spot for our seq distribution (reduced kernel switches, better KV hit amplification)
- token_budget 20: big batches, worse latency for short requests and more KV thrash on long-seq tails
sanjay: interesting. any KV cache stats? warmup effects?
maya: yes — from profiler (snippet):
```
kv_cache_hit_rate=0.68 (token_budget=8)
kv_cache_hit_rate=0.81 (token_budget=12)
kernel_switch_count=1423 (token_budget=8)
kernel_switch_count=897  (token_budget=12)
avg_batch_size=3.1 (8) vs 4.9 (12)
```
ashok: so higher token_budget both increases kv hit and reduces kernel switches. makes sense: longer lifetime per request -> more KV reuse.
leo: but why p95 regress on short requests for latency_pref? is scheduler batching those too aggressively before kernel choice returns?
maya: digging deeper — trace shows queue_policy "latency_pref" still allows 30-50ms deferral while kernel selection tries to decide between aten_fast and aten_fused. for tiny requests, that decision path plus an extra kernel load causes tail latency spikes. we see heavy path: enqueue -> wait-> kernel_choice RPC -> kernel_load -> dispatch.
sanjay: can we short-circuit kernel_choice for tiny inputs? like a pre-check: if input_len<=32 use aten_fast always.
leo: worth A/B. might be safer to add a tiny heuristic in the queue layer rather than kernel selector.
maya: proposed A/B harness config (offline):
- A: baseline (latency_pref, token_budget=8, kernel_selector=default)
- B: heuristic_shortcut (latency_pref, token_budget=12, kernel_selector=default, queue_shortcut_len=32)
also C: throughput_mix with token_budget=12 to compare throughput delta.
ashok: what about quantization/kernel binary warmup time? loading aten_fused seems to add ~18ms on first use.
maya: yes we saw cold kernel load numbers in the first 30s of each run. replay harness already includes a simulated cold-start run to capture that overhead.
leo: any perf regression signals? did we hit the regression monitor threshold?
maya: p95 regression compared to baseline exceeded 10% for short-req cohort in latency_pref+token_budget=8. filed PERF-432 for follow-up. attached perf snippet in the run meta.
replay-bot: Summary of run 1772103456: 9 experiments, 3 policy variants, token_budget targets [8,12,20]. Best compromise: latency-pref + token_budget=12 + queue_shortcut_len=32 reduces p95 by ~70ms vs baseline while keeping throughput within 5%.
ashok: next steps: (1) add queue_shortcut heuristic to branch in queue policy, (2) run A/B offline with real traces for 48h, (3) add microbenchmark to confirm kernel cold-load penalty, (4) sanity-run on Dedicated to validate GPU variance.
maya: I'll add the patch for queue_shortcut and schedule the A/B in the replay harness. dropping the full artifacts in /artifacts/replay/17721. ping me if you want early access. :thumbsup:
